title: Min Cost to Connect All Points
statement: You get points on a flat grid as [x, y] pairs. Linking two points costs the Manhattan distance: |x1 - x2| + |y1 - y2|. Link the points with cables so that every point can reach every other one, as cheaply as possible. Return that minimum total cost.

example.caption: Five points, four cables, total cost 20. Each cable is labelled with its Manhattan distance.

idea.sentence: Grow one connected group from a start point, and each time add the outside point that is cheapest to link to the group.

jargon.plain: The cheapest set of links that connects every point. With n points it has exactly n-1 links and no loops.
Distance when you can only move along the grid: horizontal steps plus vertical steps.
Build the tree from one point outward, always taking the cheapest link that leaves the tree.

watch.inputHint: One argument: a list of [x, y] points, e.g. [[0,0],[2,2],[3,10],[5,2],[7,0]]

compare.unit: checks (rough; real brute force is far worse)

rows.name: Try every set of links
rows.note: There are n(n-1)/2 possible links. Choosing n-1 of them blows up fast.

rows.name: Prim with a cost array
rows.note: n rounds. Each round scans for the cheapest outside point and updates costs. Good for a complete graph.

rows.name: Kruskal with union-find
rows.note: Sort all n^2/2 links, then join groups. Not shown. Slower here because the graph is complete.

fast.takeaway: Every point can reach every other, so the graph is dense. A plain array scan beats a heap, because the heap would hold about n^2 links.

stages.title: Start the tree
stages.note: Point 0 joins for free. Every other point has no known link yet, so its cost is infinity.

stages.title: Pick the cheapest outside point
stages.note: Scan the points not yet in the tree. The one with the smallest cost joins, and its cost is added to the total.

stages.title: Update costs
stages.note: The new tree point may be closer to an outside point than any earlier tree point. If so, lower that point's cost.

stages.title: Return the total
stages.note: After n rounds all points are connected. The sum of the costs paid is the answer.

edges.title: One point
edges.why: Nothing to connect. Point 0 joins for free and the loop ends.

edges.title: Points in a line
edges.why: The cheapest cables join neighbours only. Jumping from 0 straight to 3 costs 3 by itself and still leaves others out.

edges.title: Very far apart
edges.why: Negative coordinates are fine because of the absolute values. The total can reach about 4 million times n, which still fits in an int.

edges.title: Cheap link updated later
edges.why: Point 3 first looks 7 away through point 0, then only 3 away through point 1. The update step is what finds that.

gotchas.text: Only update an outside point's cost, never a point already in the tree. Its cost was paid and is final.
Prim needs a single connected start. Because every pair of points can be linked, point 0 reaches everyone and no connectivity check is needed.
Infinity works as 'no link yet' in comparisons, but it turns into null in JSON. Never put raw Infinity into anything you serialise or display.
math.MaxInt as 'no link yet' is safe here because it is only compared, never added to. Adding to it would overflow to a negative number and win every comparison.
There is no built-in integer abs. math.Abs takes and returns float64, so write a small abs(x int) helper.

recap.key: Keep the cheapest link into the tree for every outside point, add the cheapest point, then refresh the links.
moves: Start the tree at point 0 with cost 0
Pick the outside point with the smallest cost
Add its cost, then lower other costs via the new point
Repeat n times and return the total
